question: Has Workday announced any restructuring recently? What are the details and expected costs?
grading: Reference-free (no fixed answer), graded for recency and support. Expect: announced 2026-09-29; reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of the workforce, primarily in Product and Technology, plus select leased office space reductions; estimated charges USD 65M-80M (about USD 55M-70M in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10M in Q4 FY2027); fiscal 2027 Q3 and full-year guidance reiterated except GAAP operating margin. Snapshot as of 2026-10-03.
answer: On September 29, 2026 Workday disclosed in an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 2.05) that certain functions announced reorganizations including a reduction of approximately 2.5% of its workforce, primarily within the Product and Technology team, and select leased office space reductions, while continuing to hire in strategic areas. It estimates charges of about USD 65-80 million, of which about USD 55-70 million in Q3 FY2027 and about USD 10 million in Q4 FY2027 (roughly USD 40-55 million future cash for severance and benefits, about USD 10 million non-cash stock-based compensation and about USD 15 million non-cash lease impairment). Workday reiterated its Q3 and full-year FY2027 guidance from August 27 except GAAP operating margin (now about 20-21 points below non-GAAP in Q3 and about 19 points below for the full year). [T16-E1, T16-E2] Separately, on October 1, 2026 Workday entered into a new USD 1.5 billion revolving credit agreement replacing its USD 1.0 billion 2022 facility; this is not part of the restructuring. [T16-E3]

output.answer:
Yes. Workday announced a restructuring in early February, saying it will eliminate roughly \*\*400 jobs\*\*—about 2% of its workforce—mostly in non-revenue-generating roles on its Global Customer Operations team.

**Expected costs**
The company estimates the restructuring will result in approximately **$135 million** in charges, broken down as follows:

* **~$40 million** in cash expenditures for severance, employee benefits, and related costs
* **~$15 million** in non-cash charges for stock-based compensation
* **~$80 million** in non-cash charges related to the impairment of certain office space and long-lived assets

**Impact**
Workday warned that these charges will significantly dampen near-term profitability: GAAP operating margins are expected to be **24–25 percentage points lower** for the quarter and **22–23 percentage points lower** for the full fiscal year. The restructuring is expected to be largely completed by late April 2026.

**Context / previous round**
This is the company’s second major cut in roughly a year. In February 2025, Workday laid off about **1,750 employees** (8.5% of staff) as it shifted focus toward AI and international expansion. That earlier restructuring was followed by a leadership change in February—the company announced CEO Carl Eschenbach was stepping down and co-founder Aneel Bhusri would return to the role.

Sources:
* [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/02/04/workday-layoffs-to-hit-about-400-jobs/4983582)
* [TechRepublic](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-workday-cuts-400-jobs)
* [HR Executive](https://hrexecutive.com/workday-files-more-job-cuts-customer-ops-teams-hit)
* [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/recent-company-layoffs-laying-off-workers-2025)
* [The Register (CEO)](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/02/09/workday-ceo-steps-down-amid-layoffs-and-market-jitters/4539088)
